subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Independent Training Cycle: Plan, Execute, Adjust
title: Investigation or close reading: planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised under transfer
focus: planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised
essentialQuestion: Can I run a full cycle without anyone checking on me?
materials: Optional: two soft household objects may mark a path. Floor tape, cones, a track, and a gym are not required.
Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
movementCues: Begin in a ready position with a balanced base, soft knees, eyes up, and the travel path clear.
Move with quiet, controlled steps or wheel pushes and keep enough room to stop without crossing the boundary.
Change direction by slowing first, lowering the center of control, and pushing smoothly into the new path.
Finish under control inside the space; smooth starts, stops, and spacing matter more than speed.
Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
spaceSetup: Clear a dry, non-slip area at least two arm-spans wide when available. Mark the boundary with visible household objects or imaginary lines, remove furniture, cords, pets, and breakables, and keep a stable chair or wall nearby if support helps. Low-space path: clear one arm-span while seated or standing and keep every movement in place.

optional: Optional: two soft household objects may mark a path. Floor tape, cones, a track, and a gym are not required.
householdSubstitutes: Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm patterns to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions, then name the cue that kept the movement controlled. Full transfer credit requires evidence from every stage of the cycle, including the pre-committed adjustment rules and the decision made at each review point. Executing or fully modelling the cycle earns equal credit when the complete decision record is present.

safetyRules: Check the floor, ceiling, footwear or mobility supports, boundary, and any optional item before moving. Keep people, pets, furniture, cords, and breakables outside the boundary.
Use a self-selected easy-to-moderate challenge, breathe continuously, and choose control over speed, force, distance, or repetition.
Rest, reduce range or pace, use support, or choose the non-movement planning path at any time without losing credit.
Keep the pace below running indoors unless a trusted adult has approved a larger clear area. Use no jumping when the surface, ceiling, footwear, or balance support is uncertain.
stoppingRules: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, or any movement that feels unsafe; tell a trusted adult.
Stop when a person, pet, object, or slippery surface enters the movement area. Reset the area before continuing.
After a head impact, injury, or symptoms that do not settle with rest, do not resume the activity until a trusted adult or qualified professional says it is safe.
accessibleAdaptation: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit. Full transfer credit requires evidence from every stage of the cycle, including the pre-committed adjustment rules and the decision made at each review point. Executing or fully modelling the cycle earns equal credit when the complete decision record is present.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm patterns to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions, then name the cue that kept the movement controlled. Full transfer credit requires evidence from every stage of the cycle, including the pre-committed adjustment rules and the decision made at each review point. Executing or fully modelling the cycle earns equal credit when the complete decision record is present.
activitySteps: Setup: read the equipment, space, safety, stop, and transfer-evidence rules; clear the area and choose the standard or adapted path.
Prepare: begin with comfortable joint movements or a low-intensity rehearsal of the planned evidence while breathing normally.
Practice: apply the movement cues for planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised at a self-selected challenge, resting or reducing the range whenever control changes.

Apply: perform, simulate, diagram, gesture, or fully describe planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised under the authored transfer condition and preserve every required cue, decision, comparison, or revision. Full transfer credit requires evidence from every stage of the cycle, including the pre-committed adjustment rules and the decision made at each review point. Executing or fully modelling the cycle earns equal credit when the complete decision record is present.
Finish: transition to easy movement or rest, then name one safety check and one adjustment for next time. No score, measurement, photo, or recording is needed beyond the stated transfer evidence.
privacySafeScenario: Run a complete self-directed training cycle end to end, documenting every adjustment and its reason, and write an honest evaluation of what worked and what did not.
studentTask: Learner works planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised carried independently through a guardian-approved cycle or a fully modelled cycle, with the pre-committed rules honoured rather than renegotiated at each stage at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one. Full transfer credit requires evidence from every stage of the cycle, including the pre-committed adjustment rules and the decision made at each review point. Executing or fully modelling the cycle earns equal credit when the complete decision record is present.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner clears or accurately describes the safe space and selects the standard, accessible, or no-equipment path for planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised.

The learner performs or fully models planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised under the authored transfer condition and supplies the stated cue, decision, comparison, or revision evidence. Full transfer credit requires evidence from every stage of the cycle, including the pre-committed adjustment rules and the decision made at each review point. Executing or fully modelling the cycle earns equal credit when the complete decision record is present.
The learner identifies the equipment choice (including none), one safety or stop rule, and one technique adjustment or next step.

A seated, supported, reduced-range, solo, low-space, no-equipment, simulated, diagrammed, or described version earns equal credit only when it preserves the same transfer evidence. Full transfer credit requires evidence from every stage of the cycle, including the pre-committed adjustment rules and the decision made at each review point. Executing or fully modelling the cycle earns equal credit when the complete decision record is present.
adaptationChoices: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit. Full transfer credit requires evidence from every stage of the cycle, including the pre-committed adjustment rules and the decision made at each review point. Executing or fully modelling the cycle earns equal credit when the complete decision record is present.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Goal, modality, and volume are the learner’s; any medical restriction is planned around with guardian input.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
